## 1 Abstract

[`dmai_app()`](https://myaseen208.com/dmai/reference/dmai_app.md) opens
an application in the web browser that computes monetary aggregates
without code: the data and its columns, one index with its weights and
user costs, every method side by side, the user costs and the Divisia
second moments. This vignette describes its pages and how it keeps its
results reproducible.

## 2 Starting the application

``` r

dmai_app(
    launch.browser = TRUE
  )
```

The application needs the suggested packages **shiny**, **bslib** and
**DT**. **magick** with WebP support is optional: with it the plots are
sent to the browser as WebP images, smaller than the same PNG.

## 3 The pages

| Page | What it does |
|----|----|
| Home | what the application does and the order of the pages |
| Data | the simulated example `money_sim` or a CSV file with one row per date; the date, quantity and rate columns (in the same order), the benchmark rate (a column, or the largest component rate) and whether the rates are in percent |
| Index | one method (Divisia, Divisia with simple growth, Fisher, simple sum, currency equivalent), the value at the first date and the logarithm of the growth; interpretation, plot, table, printed output and R code |
| Compare | the chosen methods side by side, as indexes or growth rates |
| User costs | the user cost and weight of every component over time |
| Second moments | the Divisia variance of the growth of the components |
| References | the articles behind the methods, as [`dmai_cite()`](https://myaseen208.com/dmai/reference/dmai_cite.md) prints them |

Every result page has the same tabs:

- **Interpretation** gives the plain-language reading of
  [`dmai_interpret()`](https://myaseen208.com/dmai/reference/dmai_interpret.md),
  with a button that copies it.
- **Plot** shows the figure, which can be saved as PNG, PDF or WebP.
- **Table** shows the numbers, rounded, in a sortable table with buttons
  to copy them or save them as CSV or Excel.
- **Output** shows the printed result as text, with a button that copies
  it.

The index page has a further tab, **R code**, with the code that
reproduces the result outside the application.

## 4 Reproducibility

For the settings of the screenshots, the R code tab shows:

``` r

settings <-
  list(
      source  = "example"
    , method  = "Barnett"
    , logbase = "e"
    , date    = "Date"
    , x       = paste0("x", 1:8)
    , r       = paste0("r", 1:8)
    , bench   = "rb"
    , percent = TRUE
    , base    = 100
    )
cat(dmai:::.dmai_app_code(input = settings))
```

    library(dmai)
    data(money_sim)
    dat <- money_sim
    fit <-
      dmai(
          .data     = dat
        , method    = "Barnett"
        , logbase   = NULL
        , date      = "Date"
        , x         = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7", "x8")
        , r         = c("r1", "r2", "r3", "r4", "r5", "r6", "r7", "r8")
        , user_cost = NULL
        , benchmark = "rb"
        , percent   = TRUE
        , base      = 100
        , as_dt     = FALSE
        )
    fit
    plot(x = fit)
    dmai_interpret(
        x   = fit
      , top = 3
      )

The indexes are deterministic, so the code returns the same numbers as
the application.

## 5 Deploying

[`dmai_app_object()`](https://myaseen208.com/dmai/reference/dmai_app.md)
returns the application object without running it, for a server:

``` r

# app.R on a Shiny server
dmai::dmai_app_object()
```

## 6 References

Barnett, W. A. (1980). Economic monetary aggregates: an application of
index number and aggregation theory. *Journal of Econometrics*, 14(1),
11–48.
